questions.q: How does the typical bank statement import file differ from the other FBDI loads covered in this chapter?
options: It doesn't differ at all — it always uses the same Oracle Excel template
It can only be entered manually, one transaction at a time
The file usually originates outside Oracle Fusion, produced by the bank itself in a standardized banking format, rather than an Oracle-published template you fill in
It requires no interface table at all
questions.explain: Unlike supplier, journal, invoice, or receivables templates, bank statement files are typically produced by the bank itself in a standard format, not filled in by the user on an Oracle template.

An Oracle Fusion-specific Excel template

A scheduled process name
questions.explain: BAI2 is a standardized format from the Bank Administration Institute used by banks to produce statement files, independent of Oracle Fusion.

questions.q: Which interface table does bank statement data stage into within Cash Management?
options: GL_INTERFACE
FA_MASS_ADDITIONS
RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL
CE_STATEMENT_HEADERS_INT
questions.explain: CE_STATEMENT_HEADERS_INT is the Cash Management statement staging table, with corresponding line-level staging for individual transactions.

questions.q: Why is a correctly loaded bank statement necessary for Cash Management reconciliation?
options: It isn't necessary — reconciliation works entirely from internal records alone
It provides the external source of truth that reconciliation compares against your own recorded deposits, payments, and fees
It automatically deletes all internal transaction records
It replaces the need for a chart of accounts
questions.explain: Reconciliation depends on comparing your internal transaction records against an external source of truth — the bank's own statement, once loaded.

questions.q: Why are bank statement imports typically run on a recurring cadence rather than as a one-time conversion?
options: Because Oracle requires it to be run exactly once per year
Because bank statements never contain useful data
Because ongoing cash reconciliation depends on statements being loaded regularly, unlike a one-time supplier or journal conversion
Because a one-time load is technically impossible for this module
questions.explain: Unlike a one-time go-live conversion, bank statement loading supports ongoing operational reconciliation, so it needs to happen on a predictable, recurring schedule.
